You are a helpful chemistry assistant. You build 3D molecular
  structures from the chemical information you are given, including 2D drawings
  supplied as images.

  When you are given a 2D drawing of a molecule, your task is to produce the 3D
  structure that drawing depicts and save it as `answer.xyz` in your working
  directory.

  Requirements for `answer.xyz`:
  - Include all explicit hydrogens.
  - Use a right-handed Cartesian coordinate system, units of angstroms.
  - Standard XYZ format: first line is the total atom count, second line a
    one-line comment, each remaining line `Element X Y Z`.

  When you are done, confirm that `answer.xyz` exists in the working directory.

A 2D structure of a molecule is provided as a PNG file in your working directory: mol_0174.png

Build the 3D structure it depicts and save it as answer.xyz.

cat > build.py <<'PY'
from rdkit import Chem
from rdkit.Chem import AllChem
import numpy as np

# atom indices match locations in the supplied chemical diagram
atoms=['C','C','C','C','C','C','O','O','C','C','N','C','O','N','C','C','C','C','C','N','C','C','N','N','C','O','C','C','Cl','C','C','C','N','C','O','C','O','C','C','O','S','O','O','O']
xy=[(419,163),(316,102),(211,163),(211,283),(316,343),(419,283),(145,126),(145,321),(534,124),(599,221),(535,326),(728,221),(765,129),(766,325),(903,325),(963,430),(1082,430),(1155,332),(1267,369),(1267,491),(1155,526),(1366,563),(1473,519),(1352,669),(568,425),(688,425),(510,538),(395,538),(343,469),(336,634),(267,680),(319,707),(565,643),(510,745),(394,745),(566,848),(525,921),(420,967),(691,848),(751,745),(809,746),(846,674),(848,816),(900,746)]
# sulfur ester  -CH2-O-S(=O)(=O)[O-]
edge=[(0,1,1),(1,2,1),(2,3,1),(3,4,1),(4,5,1),(5,0,1),(2,6,1),(3,7,1), (0,8,1),(8,9,1),(9,10,1),(10,5,1),(9,11,1),(11,12,2),(11,13,1),(13,14,1),(14,15,1),(15,16,1),(16,17,2),(17,18,1),(18,19,1),(19,20,1),(20,16,1),(19,21,2),(21,22,1),(21,23,1),(10,24,1),(24,25,2),(24,26,1),(26,27,1),(27,28,1),(27,29,1),(29,30,1),(29,31,1),(26,32,1),(32,33,1),(33,34,2),(33,35,1),(35,36,1),(36,37,1),(35,38,1),(38,39,1),(39,40,1),(40,41,2),(40,42,2),(40,43,1)]
rw=Chem.RWMol()
for idx,el in enumerate(atoms):
    a=Chem.Atom(el)
    if idx==19: a.SetFormalCharge(1)
    if idx==43: a.SetFormalCharge(-1)
    rw.AddAtom(a)
for a,b,btype in edge:
    rw.AddBond(a,b,{1:Chem.BondType.SINGLE,2:Chem.BondType.DOUBLE}[btype])
mol=rw.GetMol()
Chem.SanitizeMol(mol)
print('nonchiral smiles:', Chem.MolToSmiles(mol))
mol=Chem.AddHs(mol)
print('atoms:', mol.GetNumAtoms())
# Right-handed xyz coordinates: x to right of picture, y upward, z out toward viewer.
conf=Chem.Conformer(mol.GetNumAtoms())
conf.Set3D(True)
for i,(x,y) in enumerate(xy):conf.SetAtomPosition(i, (x*.01,-y*.01,0))
mol.AddConformer(conf)
# Bring wedged groups toward viewer and dashed groups behind drawing.
for idx,z in {6:.9,7:-.9,28:.9,32:-.9,36:.9}.items():
    p=np.array(conf.GetAtomPosition(idx));p[2]=z;conf.SetAtomPosition(idx,p)
# Assign artificial stereocenter hydrogen placement to reproduce shown stereobonds:
centers=[0,2,3,5,26,27,35]
for cent in centers:
    hs=[n.GetIdx() for n in mol.GetAtomWithIdx(cent).GetNeighbors() if n.GetSymbol()=='H']
    assert len(hs)==1,(cent,hs)
    h=hs[0]
    p=np.array(conf.GetAtomPosition(cent))
    if cent in (0,5):
        # the diagram explicitly shows the two bridgehead hydrogens dashed back.
        hxy=(419,60) if cent==0 else (419,391)
        hp=np.array([hxy[0]*.01, -hxy[1]*.01,-.9])
    else:
        hv=np.array([np.array(conf.GetAtomPosition(j.GetIdx()))-p for j in mol.GetAtomWithIdx(cent).GetNeighbors() if j.GetIdx()!=h])
        # implicit H occupies opposite side to wedged substituent
        hp=p-np.sum(hv/np.linalg.norm(hv,axis=1)[:,None],axis=0)*.75
    conf.SetAtomPosition(h,hp)
Chem.AssignAtomChiralTagsFromStructure(mol,replaceExistingTags=True)
for a in mol.GetAtoms():
    if a.GetIdx() not in centers:a.SetChiralTag(Chem.ChiralType.CHI_UNSPECIFIED)
Chem.AssignStereochemistry(mol,force=True,cleanIt=True)
print('assigned stereocenters:',[(i, str(mol.GetAtomWithIdx(i).GetChiralTag()),mol.GetAtomWithIdx(i).GetProp('_CIPCode') if mol.GetAtomWithIdx(i).HasProp('_CIPCode') else '?') for i in centers])
print('chiral smiles:', Chem.MolToSmiles(Chem.RemoveHs(mol),isomericSmiles=True))
# Replace stretched 2D conformer by genuine low energy conformers; unassigned stereocenter 9 is arbitrary.
mol.RemoveAllConformers()
params=AllChem.ETKDGv3();params.randomSeed=170174;params.numThreads=4;params.maxIterations=250
ids=AllChem.EmbedMultipleConfs(mol,numConfs=24,params=params)
print('successful embeds:',len(ids))
if not ids:raise ValueError('Could not embed molecule')
props=AllChem.MMFFGetMoleculeProperties(mol)
if props:
    opt=AllChem.MMFFOptimizeMoleculeConfs(mol,numThreads=4,maxIters=350,mmffVariant='MMFF94s')
    print('MMFF lowest:', sorted(opt,key=lambda x:x[1])[:4]); idx=min(range(len(ids)),key=lambda i: opt[i][1])
else:
    opt=AllChem.UFFOptimizeMoleculeConfs(mol,numThreads=4,maxIters=350)
    print('UFF lowest:', sorted(opt,key=lambda x:x[1])[:4]);idx=min(range(len(ids)),key=lambda i: opt[i][1])
conf=mol.GetConformer(ids[idx])
with open('answer.xyz','w') as f:
    f.write(str(mol.GetNumAtoms())+'\n')
    f.write('Stereospecific 3D molecular structure from mol_0174.png\n')
    for a in mol.GetAtoms():
        p=conf.GetAtomPosition(a.GetIdx())
        f.write(f'{a.GetSymbol():2s} {p.x: .7f} {p.y: .7f} {p.z: .7f}\n')
print('wrote answer.xyz; charge:', Chem.GetFormalCharge(mol), 'selected conformer:',idx)
PY
python build.py

    ff=AllChem.UFFGetMoleculeForceField(mol,confId=ids[idx])
print('Refinement:', status, 'energy:', ff.CalcEnergy())
conf=mol.GetConformer(ids[idx])
check=Chem.Mol(mol)
Chem.AssignAtomChiralTagsFromStructure(check,confId=ids[idx],replaceExistingTags=True)
Chem.AssignStereochemistry(check,force=True,cleanIt=True)
assert all(check.GetAtomWithIdx(i).GetProp('_CIPCode')==mol.GetAtomWithIdx(i).GetProp('_CIPCode') for i in centers)
with open('answer.xyz','w') as f:""")
open(p,'w').write(s)
